evidence: p89: "Prefill takes about 1.08 s, while generating the 300-token answer takes about 7.5 s"; p90: "prefill (~1.08 s for 9,200 tokens across the 8×H100 canonical host, ≈8.5K tokens/s prefill — below the host’s ~19,800 tok/s sustained-planning prefill rate"; p101: "But it is only ~15% of the wall-clock time (1.08 s prefill vs 6.0 s decode)"

Pages 89, 90 and 101 treat the budget cap as an actual prefill time, derive an "≈8.5K tokens/s prefill" rate from it, and use it for wall-clock share. This is a cross-chapter definition drift and produces numbers inconsistent with Ch 8's modeled prefill rate.
fix_instruction: Label 1.08 s explicitly as the budget cap wherever it is used. Do not write "Prefill takes about 1.08 s" or derive an actual prefill rate from it. Use the modeled host prefill time (~0.47 s at 35% MFU, ~0.16 s peak) for wall-clock/decode-share statements, or state that ≈8.5K tok/s is only the budget-implied single-request rate and not the modeled/measured prefill rate.

evidence: "With the canonical 9.2K KV re-read included, intensity saturates at ~6.8 FLOP/byte, so decode stays bandwidth-bound at every batch size — Ch 8."
issue: Under the chapter's own canonical inputs, decode arithmetic intensity including KV re-read saturates at roughly 140 GFLOP/token ÷ 24.1 GB/token ≈ 5.8 FLOP/byte (or ≈5.6 with the 24.9 GB resident basis), not ~6.8. The 6.8 value requires about 20.6 GB of KV bytes, which is not the stated canonical 9.2K FP16 KV footprint. The conclusion (bandwidth-bound) is unchanged, but the displayed derived number is inconsistent.
fix_instruction: Recompute the saturation intensity from the stated canonical KV bytes (e.g. 140 GFLOP ÷ 24.1 GB ≈ 5.8 FLOP/byte) or state the exact denominator that yields 6.8 FLOP/byte. Keep the bandwidth-bound conclusion, but align the number with the canonical KV constant.

evidence: "Controlled comparison: same context length and cache dtype — while weight residency (140 GB dense vs ~94 GB for the ~47B MoE challenger), the active-compute fraction (~100% vs ~27%) and the attention shape (canonical dense 80L/8192H full-MHA vs the challenger’s 32L/4096H GQA) all differ"

evidence: "The match is a coincidence of layout rates rather than a shared design: 4 metadata bytes per 128-value group (2 B scale + 2 B zero) and MXFP4’s 1 scale byte per 32-value group both come to 0.03125 B/value on top of the same four-bit payload."
issue: This sentence follows a packed four-bit zero-point layout (0.5 B zero/group, 8,716,288 B) and then a replacement with an FP16 scaled-zero (2 B zero/group, 8,912,896 B). The quoted 4 metadata bytes/group describes only the FP16 scaled-zero variant, not the packed-four-bit-zero variant. The referent of "this integer scheme" and "the match" is therefore ambiguous: which layout is being said to match MXFP4?
fix_instruction: Name the matching layout explicitly: state that the FP16 scaled-zero variant (8,912,896 B) happens to match MXFP4's total bytes, while the packed-four-bit-zero variant (8,716,288 B) does not. Avoid saying "this integer scheme" without naming which zero layout is meant.

evidence: "MEASURED — an instrumented run under the Chapter 14 protocol; used only where the book reports a benchmark it actually ran, never for a planning screen. ANALYTICAL — arithmetic on stated inputs … HYPOTHESIS — reasoned but not yet validated … ILLUSTRATIVE — a chosen scenario input or worked example … The four registers above are not one axis: MEASURED, ANALYTICAL and HYPOTHESIS name what was done to a number, whereas [ILLUSTRATIVE] names where it came from — so a single claim can be both ILLUSTRATIVE and ANALYTICAL."
issue: Internal contradiction in the evidence-panel definition. The panel opens by presenting 'four registers' as a unified set, then states 'The four registers above are not one axis' — denying they form one axis while having just framed them as four parallel registers. Worse, MEASURED is listed as a register in this panel, but the Preface axis note (p.19) says 'measurement status therefore uses ANALYTICAL, SCENARIO-DERIVED, MODELED, MEASURED or UNMEASURED' — i.e., MEASURED is a measurement-status value on Axis 3, not a register (the registers are Axis 1 provenance + Axis 2 epistemic status). The panel never reconciles MEASURED's dual role. Separately, ANALYTICAL appears both as one of the four 'registers' and as a measurement status on Axis 3, with no statement of whether these are the same item or two uses of one word. A reader cannot tell from this panel alone how to apply the labels correctly.
fix_instruction: Rewrite the evidence-panel opening to state plainly that two label axes (provenance, epistemic status) plus an optional measurement-status axis are used, drop the 'four registers' framing (or define exactly which axis each of the four belongs to), and add one sentence clarifying whether MEASURED and ANALYTICAL as used in the panel are the same items as the Axis-3 measurement statuses or distinct categories.

evidence: Figure 1 caption: "Two loops are drawn: the inner (green, left) returns a failed benchmark or TCO validation from 'Validate & Defend' to 'Design & size'; the outer (red, right) returns from 'Commit' to 'Understand' when a requirements revision is needed." evidence: "Every quantitative value here is one of three kinds: a dated measurement, a figure derived from cited inputs, or is explicitly identified as an illustrative assumption (see the Sources, Method, and Reproducibility chapter for the full evidence taxonomy)."

fix_instruction: Either change 'three kinds' to match the Preface's actual taxonomy (e.g., 'three provenance/status categories, with additional measurement-status labels defined in …') or add a parenthetical noting the copyright-page list is a simplified summary and the Preface/Sources chapter defines the full label set.

evidence: "A single token can be a whole word (handbook), a common subword (hand), a single character, a short punctuation+space pair, or in worst cases a single byte (a fragment of a character)." and §1.1.1: "the 'one token ≈ 4 characters' rule of thumb is for rough estimation of general-English prose, never a law" [2°][FACT].

evidence: A shared core executed several times reuses weights but repeats arithmetic. A phase-dependent architecture can also activate different paths during prefill and decode. The parameter estimate therefore needs a phase and an execution count before it enters the roofline analysis.
issue: Inconsistency with Canonical Model. Chapter 8's introduction asserts that 'The prefill pass for a single request with 9.2K input tokens... costs ~1.29 PFLOP' based on the 2xN rule (linear). This assumes the dense canonical model. However, the paragraph above explicitly warns that for 'iterative language generator' or 'diffusion-style' models, the 2N rule applies to *processed positions*, not just output tokens. While technically true, placing this warning in Section 8.1 immediately before the canonical 2N calculation in 8.3.1 might confuse readers who think the 'iterative' warning applies to the canonical RAG model (which is standard autoregressive, not iterative in that sense). The text later clarifies this is for 'alternative inference', but the juxtaposition is risky.
fix_instruction: In the paragraph starting 'A shared core executed several times...', explicitly label this as 'Alternative Inference' or 'Diffusion-style' to distinguish it clearly from the canonical autoregressive model calculation that follows.

fix_instruction: Clarify in the text that 5.6 TB/s is a *theoretical demand* if the weight read is not amortized (i.e., batch=1), and that the 'verdict' holds for batch=1 only.
